channel.title: Every Second – science posters
channel.description: Science infographic posters from the Every Second Shorts.

item.title: What If an Ant Got Twice as Strong Every Second?
item.description: An ant gets twice as strong every second: it lifts an egg at second 10, you at second 20, the Statue of Liberty at second 32 and Hoover Dam at second 46. A real ant carries about 8.78 times its own weight, not 50. But there are 20 quadrillion of them: 2.4 million for each of us.

item.title: What If a Basketball Bounced 10% Higher Every Time?
item.description: Starting from a 10 ft hoop, bounce 80 needs the speed of sound and bounce 125 reaches the space station. Real time for all of it, ignoring air: 222 minutes, and the last fall hits Mach 8.

item.title: What If Your Balloon Tripled Its Air Every Second?
item.description: You blow one breath into a balloon, and the air inside triples every second. Bigger than your lungs at second 3, an Olympic pool at second 15, the Great Pyramid at second 21, the Grand Canyon at second 34, and at second 46 it holds all the air on Earth: a balloon 1,240 miles wide.

item.title: What If a Candle Got 4 Times Stronger Every Second?
item.description: A candle releases 4 times more energy every second. Stronger than a horse at second 2, a dam at second 13, all of humanity at second 19, a hurricane at second 22, and at second 41 it shines like the Sun. The catch: it would burn a Moon's worth of wax every 2.6 hours, about 1.9 billion times more fuel than the real Sun, which runs on nuclear fusion.

item.title: What If You Photocopied Yourself Every Second?
item.description: You, photocopied every second, and every copy too: 18 seconds to fill the world's biggest stadium, 33 to outnumber humanity, and at second 61 your copies burn all of Earth's oxygen in a single day.

item.title: What If Your Coffee Got 10% Hotter Every Second?
item.description: From 140°F, 10% more every second on the Celsius scale: it melts lead at second 18, beats the Sun at second 48 and lightning at second 65, when one cup radiates 0.85 GW, about a nuclear reactor.

item.title: What If Your Coin Landed Heads Every Second?
item.description: A coin, flipped every second, and it always lands on heads: after 29 seconds it's less likely than winning the biggest US lottery, after 33 it's harder than finding one person in the world, and by second 59 it's harder than picking a single second since the Big Bang.

item.title: What If a Submarine Dove 17% Deeper Every Second?
item.description: A tiny sub dives 17% deeper every second, starting 3 feet down: it passes the recreational scuba limit at second 24, beats the scuba world record at second 37, outdives every whale at second 51 and passes the Titanic at second 53. Then the rule asks for 40,470 feet, but the ocean ends at 35,876 feet, where every square inch carries 8 tons of water.

item.title: What If Your Dollar Doubled Every Second?
item.description: $1 doubling every second buys a new car at second 16, passes all the wealth on Earth at second 49 and could make everyone a billionaire at second 63.

item.title: What If Every Domino Was 50% Bigger Than the Last?
item.description: Each domino is 50% bigger than the one before, and one falls every second. Domino 15 is taller than you, domino 30 is taller than the Burj Khalifa, and domino 42 reaches space. The craziest part: a domino really can knock over one 1.5 times its size.

item.title: What If Your Eyesight Got 30% Sharper Every Second?
item.description: Your eyesight gets 30% sharper every second. At second 4 you see like an eagle, at second 17 you could spot a person from the space station, at second 28 you beat the Hubble telescope, and at second 55 you can see a black hole. The catch: physics says your pupil would then need to be 2.6 miles wide.

item.title: What If the Sea Rose 40% Higher Every Second?
item.description: The sea starts 0.4 inches high and rises 40% more every second: at second 38 it needs more water than Earth has, at 41 it covers Everest, at 53 it wets the space station, and at 60 the ocean outweighs the planet.

item.title: What If One Bacterium Doubled Every Second?
item.description: One E. coli bacterium weighs about a picogram. What if it split in two every second? It outweighs a red blood cell at second 7, a grain of salt at second 26, a mosquito at second 32, a mouse at second 45, and at second 56 the pile weighs as much as you. Real E. coli takes about 20 minutes per split: at that pace, it would outweigh the Earth in 44 hours. It never does, because the food runs out first.

item.title: What If Gravity Got 40% Stronger Every Second?
item.description: A 100 g apple on a kitchen scale, with gravity up 40% every second: second 20 it weighs as much as an adult, second 27 the atmosphere is 1 m high, and second 61 escape velocity passes the speed of light. Earth becomes a black hole with its radius unchanged.

item.title: What If Your Heart Beat 12% Faster Every Second?
item.description: Your heart beats 12% faster every second, starting at a calm 60 bpm: past a 20-year-old's maximum heart rate at second 11, faster than a mouse at second 21, and at second 27 it beats so fast you can hear it as a hum. Then it outruns a shrew, a hummingbird's wings and a bumblebee, until it plays the exact note an orchestra tunes to.

item.title: What If an Ice Cube Lost 7°F Every Second?
item.description: An ice cube at 32°F gets 7.2°F (4°C) colder every second: it freezes mercury at second 10, breaks Earth's cold record at second 23, makes the air rain down at second 46 and reaches absolute zero, -459.67°F, at second 69.

item.title: What If Light Lost 35% of Its Speed Every Second?
item.description: Light loses 35% of its speed every second: video calls lag after 7 seconds, a space probe overtakes it at second 18, you can walk faster than light at second 45, and by second 62 even a snail wins.

item.title: What If a Fridge Magnet Got 50% Stronger Every Second?
item.description: A fridge magnet gets 50% stronger every second. At second 16 it's an MRI, at second 20 it can levitate a frog, at second 33 it beats the strongest field ever made on Earth, and at second 44 atoms stretch into needles. And a magnetar is still 357,000 times stronger.

item.title: What If the Moon Got 5% Closer Every Second?
item.description: The Moon moves 5% closer every second: at second 23 the tide beats the highest on Earth, at 44 it hangs still in the sky, and at 60 Earth's gravity tears it apart. The rings that follow are how it was born.

item.title: What If a Mosquito Doubled in Size Every Second?
item.description: A 5 mm mosquito doubling in size every second: at second 7 one bite takes all your blood, at 9 it hits the ceiling, at 32 it's bigger than Earth, and at 63 it touches the nearest star.

item.title: What If You Folded Paper Once More Every Second?
item.description: Every fold doubles a 0.1 mm sheet: fold 42 passes the Moon, fold 69 reaches the nearest star, about 10x thinner than an atom.

item.title: What If a Pepper Got 40% Hotter Every Second?
item.description: A pepperoncini at 500 SHU gets 40% hotter every second: it beats any jalapeño at second 9, the ghost pepper at second 23, the Pepper X world record at second 26, pure capsaicin at second 31, and at second 52 it reaches the hottest substance known, which doesn't even come from a pepper.

item.title: What If You Cut a Pizza Into 4 Every Second?
item.description: Cut a pizza into 4 every second and keep only one piece. At cut 8 it weighs less than a grain of rice, at cut 25 less than a bacterium, and at cut 43 your piece is a single atom. That's when the knife has to stop: in Greek, "atom" literally means "uncuttable".

item.title: What If a Hydraulic Press Pushed 40% Harder Every Second?
item.description: A hydraulic press pushes 40% harder every second on a block of graphite, the stuff in pencils. Espresso pressure at second 7, steel starts to flow at second 24, diamond-making pressure at second 33, and at second 45 it matches the center of the Earth. The twist: labs reach that pressure every day with two tiny diamonds and the force of a 25 lb weight.

item.title: What If One Grain of Rice Doubled Every Second?
item.description: One 25 mg grain, doubled every second: 28 seconds for an elephant, 43 for a giant cargo ship, 443 years of world harvests on the 64th chessboard square, and at second 66 a pile taller than Everest, or one layer of grains over the whole Earth.

item.title: What If Your Shoelace Doubled in Length Every Second?
item.description: A sneaker lace is about 47 inches long. Now double it every second: longer than a bus at second 4, taller than Everest at 13, Paris to London at 19, around the Earth at 25, to the Moon at 29, to the Sun at 37, and at 45 it reaches Voyager 1, which just became the first probe one light-day from Earth. By then light needs 39 hours to cross it, and its tip has been outrunning light since second 29.

item.title: What If Everyone Who Heard Your Secret Told 2 New People?
item.description: You tell a secret to 2 people, one per second, and everyone who hears it does the same. Your whole class knows at second 6, the biggest cruise ship at 18, New York City at 32, India at 43 and every person on Earth at second 47. Then there's nobody left to tell, except the 4 babies born every second.

item.title: What If Your Sneeze Got 50% Faster Every Second?
item.description: A real sneeze tops out around 10 mph. Now make it 50% faster every second: it outruns a cheetah at second 5, breaks the sound barrier at 11, leaves Earth for good at 20, beats the fastest spacecraft at 27 and reaches the Moon in 1.5 seconds at 44. At second 45 it would have to outrun light. The universe says: bless you.

item.title: What If a Snowball Got 60% Heavier Every Second?
item.description: A snowball gets 60% heavier every second as it rolls downhill: it outweighs you after 13 seconds, a blue whale at second 29, the Eiffel Tower at second 38 and the Great Pyramid at second 52. But a snowball can only grow by eating snow: by the end it has swallowed 3 feet of snow from 5,300 soccer fields.

item.title: What If Earth Spun 5% Faster Every Second?
item.description: Earth spins 5% faster every second: at second 31 the equator outruns the X-15 rocket plane, at second 51 you weigh half as much there, and at second 59 the equator weighs nothing at all.

item.title: What If Water Got 3 Times Thicker Every Second?
item.description: Water gets 3 times thicker every second: olive oil at second 4, honey at second 9, pitch (one drop per decade) at second 24, thicker than granite at second 48, and by second 51 it is as thick as Earth's mantle, which still flows under your feet about as fast as your fingernails grow.

item.title: What If Time Went Twice as Fast Every Second?
item.description: Time runs twice as fast every second: one second lasts an hour at second 12, a whole year at second 25, longer than a human life at second 32, and the dinosaurs died less than a second ago at second 51. At second 59, a single second lasts longer than the universe has existed.

item.title: What If a AA Battery Gained 37% More Voltage Every Second?
item.description: A tiny 1.5 V battery gains 37% voltage every second: it beats a car battery at second 7, the most electric eel on Earth at second 21, the biggest US power lines at second 42, and at second 61 it holds the voltage of a lightning bolt. By then, that one AA could power an average US home for 89 years.

item.title: What If Your Speaker Doubled Its Power Every Second?
item.description: A speaker starts at 20 dB and doubles its power every second: at second 34 it can harm your ears at once, at 51 it matches Krakatoa, and at 58 the air cannot carry a louder sound.

item.title: What If You Walked 40% Faster Every Second?
item.description: A 3 mph walk gaining 40% every second breaks the sound barrier at second 17, leaves Earth at second 27, passes the Moon at second 55 and hits light speed at second 58, 554,000 miles from home.

item.title: What If Your Wi-Fi Got Twice as Fast Every Second?
item.description: Your internet starts at 1 bit per second and doubles every second. A text message at second 11, the Apollo 11 computer's entire memory at second 20, an HD movie at second 36, all of Wikipedia at second 38, and the whole internet's traffic at second 52. The catch: a 128 GB phone was full at second 39, so it kept only 0.003% of everything.

item.title: What If the Wind Blew 15% Harder Every Second?
item.description: The wind starts at 6 mph and blows 15% harder every second: at second 35 it breaks the sound barrier, at 40 it beats Neptune's winds, and at 60 the air reaches escape velocity and leaves Earth.

item.title: What If You Zoomed In 2x Every Second?
item.description: Start with your hand and zoom in twice as close every second. Your fingerprint at second 3, a skin cell at second 10, a bacterium at second 16, DNA at second 24, a carbon atom at second 28... and then 15 seconds of nothing before the nucleus. If the nucleus were 1 cm wide, the atom would span 2.7 soccer fields: it is 99.9999999999956% empty space.
